_about: Every column of data/derived/lift_days.csv: its role, when it is known (as-of), unit, source and interval. scripts/check_data.py fails if a column is missing here. 'full-day hindsight' features describe the day and must not be presented as a morning prediction. Time convention: weather-file clock is unlabelled by the vendor; see docs/DATA_SOURCES.md section 13.

winter.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

date.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

lift.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

side.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

scheduled.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

in_season.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

covid_era.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

n_posts_day.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

in_heldout_posts.note: identifies the lift-day or how it was selected

early_gust.source: wwg 15-minute ridge stations (Siberia, Summit, Roundhouse Top, Scott Top, Belmont, Funitel Top)
early_gust.interval: maximum 15-minute gust (or sustained speed) over local 05:00-09:00, all ridge stations

early_spd.source: wwg 15-minute ridge stations (Siberia, Summit, Roundhouse Top, Scott Top, Belmont, Funitel Top)
early_spd.interval: maximum 15-minute gust (or sustained speed) over local 05:00-09:00, all ridge stations

day_gust.interval: maximum over local 06:00-16:00, all ridge stations
day_gust.note: includes hours after the hold: describes the day, does not predict it

day_spd.interval: maximum over local 06:00-16:00, all ridge stations
day_spd.note: includes hours after the hold: describes the day, does not predict it

fnt_day_gust.source: Funitel Top station; estimated from Siberia and Belmont when the station was off or in the 2025-26 regime
fnt_day_gust.note: see fnt_src and fnt_measured; 0.0 on a windy day is treated as sensor dropout

fnt_measured.interval: as fnt_day_gust, raw reading before the dropout rule
fnt_measured.note: blank when the station had no readings

fnt_src.note: 'measured' or 'estimated' (regression on Siberia and Belmont) for fnt_day_gust

sib_h40.interval: 15-minute readings at or above 40 / 60 mph between local 06:00 and 16:00, divided by 4
sib_h40.note: blank on a Siberia dropout day

sib_h60.interval: 15-minute readings at or above 40 / 60 mph between local 06:00 and 16:00, divided by 4
sib_h60.note: blank on a Siberia dropout day

swe24.interval: change over the 24 h / 6 h before 9am local (prec24s: precipitation gauge)

swe6.interval: change over the 24 h / 6 h before 9am local (prec24s: precipitation gauge)

prec24s.interval: change over the 24 h / 6 h before 9am local (prec24s: precipitation gauge)

new_snow24.interval: depth now minus the lowest depth in the previous 24 h, 3-hourly, 5-reading medians

new_snow24_snotel.interval: sum of hourly depth increases over 24 h
new_snow24_snotel.note: older noisy figure kept for comparison

avy.asof: forecast issued the morning of the day (known at opening)
avy.source: Sierra Avalanche Center forecast, valid_day=current, max of the bands

gust_at_event.asof: at event time (first post about the lift)
gust_at_event.interval: gust and speed in the hour of the first post; strongest gust in the three hours before it
gust_at_event.note: blank without a post time; these describe the hold, not the morning

gust_prior3h.asof: at event time (first post about the lift)
gust_prior3h.interval: gust and speed in the hour of the first post; strongest gust in the three hours before it
gust_prior3h.note: blank without a post time; these describe the hold, not the morning

spd_at_event.asof: at event time (first post about the lift)
spd_at_event.interval: gust and speed in the hour of the first post; strongest gust in the three hours before it
spd_at_event.note: blank without a post time; these describe the hold, not the morning

local_station.source: rules/lift_stations.json: the station nearest each lift

local_gust.source: rules/lift_stations.json: the station nearest each lift
local_gust.note: blank on a dropout day (sensor read 0.0 while another ridge station gusted over 20 mph; data/derived/weather_qc.csv)

late_open_implied.note: a scheduled lift announced as open after 09:45 with no earlier hold, delay or closure post: an implied late opening. Kept apart from `held`; not counted as a hold

began_on_hold.note: a hold or delayed-opening post for the lift before 09:00. Evan's rule (2026-11-07): such a lift began the day on hold, so it counts as scheduled and is held from 09:00 until its reopening post

cause_first.note: cause named by the earliest hold, delay or closure event of the lift that day (the first reason it stopped); held_wind etc. are true if ANY event that day named that cause, so a lift held first for avalanche control and later for wind has cause_first=patrol and held_wind=1

closed_all_basis.note: on a whole-side closure day: 'roster' = the lift was on that day's own posts; 'window' = added because the lift had opened and not yet closed for the season (first and last day with evidence it was running or meant to run, plus 3 days); 'typical_roster_no_window' = added from the winter's typical roster because that side has too few named rosters to know the lift's window (decision 65). Blank on other days
